About Us

Preference Model is a superintelligence data research company. We build RL environments for training capable, better-aligned superintelligences.

Almost every aspect of how a model behaves is shaped by the reward signals it's trained on. The biggest problem with AIs today is that they don't always do what we intend. Sometimes that's because they aren't capable enough, and sometimes it's because they aren't aligned. Both problems come down to the training objectives.

We're trying to address both of these issues in the most direct, highest leverage way available to us, which today means researching how to build RL environments better, not just for the AIs of today but for the AIs as they will be when they outsmart us.

Over the past year, we've built RL environments for several frontier labs, and we're backed by $16M in seed funding led by a16z. Our founding team has previous experience on Anthropic’s data team building data infrastructure, and datasets behind Claude.

About The Role

An RL environment is only useful once it runs reliably inside a lab's training stack. Every environment we build has to be packaged, sandboxed, run at scale, checked against each lab's requirements, and delivered in the format that lab's platform expects. Much of that work is still manual today, and it takes time away from the people designing environments.

As an MTS on our ML Platform team
, you will own the systems that take an environment from a builder's repo to a lab's training run. That includes Karotte, our open-source framework for defining RL environments, the internal platform that builds, runs, and reviews environments on CPU, GPU, and TPU, and the integrations that deliver them to each lab we work with. This is an engineering role where you will ensure what our Capabilities team builds runs and ships cleanly.

You'll join a small Platform team and work directly with environment builders and post-training researchers. In your first six months, success looks like a delivery path to each partner lab that is mostly automated: tasks marked ready get built, validated against that lab's requirements, and packaged without hand work. Our needs change quickly, so you'll also pick up other platform and infrastructure work as priorities shift.

What You Will Do

Own the integrations that deliver our environments to partner labs: build container images, match each lab's submission format, and automate the checks that confirm requirements are met before anything ships. Do the delivery work by hand where you have to, then automate it.
Build and maintain Karotte, our open-source environment framework, from API design through releases and migrations that keep existing environments working.
Run and scale the infrastructure that builds, runs, and grades environments, including containerized rollouts and grading across CPU, GPU, and TPU, VM-based sandboxing, and the resource limits and isolation that stop a model from gaming its own grader.
Build the internal tools environment builders use every day (CLI, docs, data catalog, access controls, and run monitoring) so they spend their time on environment design instead of infrastructure.
Partner with environment builders and post-training researchers to turn recurring pain points into platform features, and ship quickly in response to their feedback.

What We are Looking For

Strong software engineering fundamentals and a track record of building and operating production infrastructure or developer platforms that other engineers depend on.
Proficiency in Python, including writing libraries and APIs that other people build on.
Hands-on experience with containers and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes, or similar) and at least one major cloud platform (GCP, AWS, or similar).
A working understanding of how to run untrusted code safely: isolation, resource limits, and what happens when a process fills the disk or refuses to exit.
Extensive hands-on use of coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or similar), and an intuition for where models cut corners.
You've owned something tedious end to end, such as a migration, a release process, or a delivery pipeline, and automated away as much of it as you could.

Position Summary

We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Senior Research Scientist. The Center for Surgical and Transplant Applied Research (CSTAR) at NYU

Langone Health is seeking a Senior Research Scientist to provide advanced scientific and methodological expertise. CSTAR is a multidisciplinary research

center dedicated to improving organ donation and transplantation through rigorous, data-driven research.

The Senior Research Scientist will lead the design and execution of complex quantitative studies using national transplant registries, electronic health

records, administrative claims, surveys, and other large healthcare datasets.

Working within the scientific framework established by CSTAR faculty and principal investigators, the Senior Research Scientist will develop analytical

strategies, address complex methodological challenges, and ensure the rigor, reproducibility, and timely completion of quantitative research projects.

The position will also contribute substantially to grant applications, manuscripts, scientific presentations, and reports and will provide senior-level guidance and

mentorship to analysts and other research staff.

Job Responsibilities

Lead the design and execution of complex statistical analyses under the direction of study

principal investigators.

Develop research questions, study designs, analytical strategies, and statistical analysis plans

for observational, clinical, health services, and outcomes research.

Apply advanced statistical methods to data from national transplant registries, electronic health

records, administrative claims, community-based surveys, project-specific assessments, and other

healthcare data sources.

Select and implement appropriate statistical methodologies, which may include survival analysis,

longitudinal analysis, multilevel modeling, causal inference, missing-data methods, predictive

modeling, and sensitivity analyses.

Independently evaluate methodological and data-related challenges and recommend scientifically

rigorous and feasible solutions.

Provide senior-level scientific oversight for data management, variable development, cohort

construction, statistical programming, model development, validation, interpretation, and

reporting.

Establish and apply standards for data quality, statistical programming, documentation,

reproducibility, and validation across projects.

Critically review analytical results to assess the validity of assumptions, identify potential

sources of bias, and ensure that findings are interpreted appropriately.

Translate clinical, scientific, and operational questions into well-defined quantitative research

studies in collaboration with principal investigators, clinicians, analysts, research staff, and

external partners.

Serve as a senior quantitative collaborator on multisite studies, national scientific committees,

and projects involving external research institutions.

Coordinate analytical activities across investigators, analysts, data managers, research teams,

and collaborating institutions.

Prepare interim and final analytical reports for principal investigators, study teams, sponsors,

data and safety monitoring boards, and other oversight groups.

Lead and contribute to the development of peer-reviewed manuscripts, abstracts, presentations,

technical reports, and other scholarly products.

Contribute to grant applications and funding proposals, including the development of study

designs, research strategies, power and sample-size calculations, analytical plans, and preliminary

analyses.

Present research findings at scientific conferences, seminars, working groups, and internal

research forums.

Provide technical and scientific guidance to data analysts, research staff, trainees, and other

members of the research team.

Train and mentor junior analysts in statistical methods, reproducible research practices, and the

appropriate use of national transplant and healthcare datasets.

Review analytical code, results, tables, figures, and written methods to ensure accuracy,

consistency, and scientific rigor.

Monitor project progress, identify analytical or operational barriers, and ensure the timely and

accurate completion of assigned deliverables.

Maintain current knowledge of advances in biostatistics, epidemiology, health services research,

transplantation research, and healthcare data science.

Ensure compliance with institutional and regulatory requirements related to research conduct,

data security, patient privacy, and the use of sensitive healthcare data.

Participate in CSTAR meetings, seminars, committees, and interdisciplinary collaborations, as

requested.

Perform other related duties as assigned.

About Us

Datasite is the essential infrastructure for M&A. Also comprising Grata, Blueflame AI, and Sherpany, we help dealbreakers find opportunities, manage transactions, and make key decisions.

Whatever your talents, you can find a place for them here. Get involved in some of the biggest business ventures today. Work with other gifted people around the world. Follow your ambitions, or discover a whole new path.

Can you help us simplify the complex, create great experiences, and deliver better outcomes? Then let's talk.

Job Description

Why Engineering at Datasite

Datasite's engineering organization builds the software the world's dealmakers depend on to find, evaluate, negotiate, and close transactions: secure virtual data rooms, AI-assisted diligence, deal sourcing, and private-company intelligence.

We’re looking for hands-on Staff Software Enginee
r to own the context AI agents use on live deals. A wrong passage, a stale document, or a missed permission becomes a wrong answer in a high-stakes workflow. You will build the retrieval layer that makes agent answers grounded, current, and secure. You will work in Python and partner closely with Product and Data Science. You will stay hands-on on the decisions that change what an agent can know.

Location
: We are hiring in New York City
and Minneapolis.
Datasite is a hybrid company, with in-office collaboration on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays.

What You Will Do

Own retrieval for agents that work on live deals. Ground each answer in the right documents and data, and set the balance of quality, speed, and cost.
Scale how the platform processes large documents and data tables, so an agent can still find and reason over content that does not fit in one pass.
Shape the context agents depend on and evolve it as deal workflows get longer and more complex.
Build the search tools agents call. Cover content that is indexed and content that is not indexed yet. Return the snippet, citation, and location a dealmaker can trust.
Keep agent context aligned with the data room and with whoever may see each item. An agent must not read content the user cannot read.
Decide when a model may answer from retrieved context and when the product must check the result.
Mentor engineers and set technical direction for retrieval across teams.

What You Bring

6+ years of building and operating production software, with a record of leading complex technical work across teams.
Strong hands-on Python, with experience in backend services, APIs, and large-scale data pipelines.
Experience with production LLM applications that depend on retrieval: tool calling, RAG, embeddings, vector search, or context management.
Strong foundations in permissions, multi-tenant data, and access control on what an agent can retrieve.
Clear product and technical judgment. You can balance answer quality, latency, and cost, and explain the tradeoffs to engineering and product leaders.

Nice to Have

Long-running agent workflows that search or read documents.
A vector store at production scale.
Processing of large confidential documents and data tables.
Hybrid search, citations, and evaluation of retrieval quality.
Virtual data rooms, M&A documents, or similar document-heavy work.
Tool interfaces that expose search to an agent.
